# Changelog

Two layers, on purpose.

**Notes** is written by hand and answers *why* a release looks the way it does:
migrations, a decision the release embodies, an interaction worth warning about.
A generated changelog answers "what landed"; only a person answers "and what
does that mean for me".

**The record** below it is generated by `cog bump` from commit subjects. Do not
edit it — it is regenerated.

Both start at `v0.1.0`, the baseline tag on the last commit written before this
repository adopted conventional commits. Nothing before that tag appears here,
and nothing before it will. See [docs/versioning.md](docs/versioning.md).

> **Editing this file by hand:** `cog bump` splices each new release
> immediately after the **first** occurrence of its separator literal — a
> Markdown thematic break written as three dashes with a space between each of
> them. Anything you add above must therefore *describe* that literal without
> *containing* it, or your release notes get spliced into the middle of your own
> prose. This has been paid for once already, in quivive 0.1.0. (The YAML front
> matter above uses an undivided three-dash fence, which is a different literal
> and is safe.)

## Notes

### Unreleased

Adopted the house conventions: a CI job that runs the same `mise run check`
you run locally, a documentation gate, three ADRs recording decisions the code
had already made, and cocogitto from here forward.

Two things to know if you work in this tree:

- **`mise run check` grew three legs** — `fmt-check`, `render` (every bundled
  sample, painted headless) and `docs` (front matter, ADR shape, dead links).
  All run locally and in CI with the same command. `fmt-check` had been held
  out because rustfmt wanted a change that buried a comment; that is fixed, so
  it is a gate again.
- **The README moved.** It answers *why* now and links out; the reference
  material it used to carry lives in [`docs/`](docs), one topic per file.
